entities.name: Hasan Buzurg
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shaikh Hasan, widely known as Hasan Buzurg or Hassan the Jalair, emerged as the founder of the Jalayirid Sultanate, a pivotal Turkic-Mongol successor state that dominated Iraq and parts of western Iran for over 80 years following the collapse of the Ilkhanate. His rise in the tumultuous mid-14th century marked a critical juncture in the political landscape of the Middle East, transitioning from unified Mongol rule to an era of competing regional dynasties. Operating from his power base in Baghdad and Tabriz, Hasan Buzurg carved out a sphere of influence amidst the fragmentation, laying the groundwork for a dynasty that would become a significant patron of Islamic arts and sciences.

Hasan Buzurg initially served as a prominent amir within the Ilkhanid administration, holding the governorship of Rum (Anatolia). Upon the death of the last effective Ilkhan, Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan, in 1335, a fierce power vacuum ensued. Hasan Buzurg navigated this treacherous period by initially supporting various puppet Ilkhanid khans, including Muhammad Khan and Jahan Temür, in a complex series of succession wars against rival factions, most notably the Chobanids under figures like Chupan and his descendants. By skillfully leveraging alliances and military force, he consolidated his control over Iraq and Azerbaijan by 1339-1340, establishing de facto independence while maintaining a nominal allegiance to a series of figurehead khans until his death in 1356, effectively ending the direct Mongol legacy in his domains.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hasan Buzurg was instrumental in establishing the Jalayirid Sultanate, one of the most enduring and culturally significant successor states after the collapse of the Ilkhanate, controlling Iraq and parts of Iran for over 80 years. His actions defined the regional political landscape for generations and fostered a unique blend of Mongol and Persianate culture.
